Look Up Values Stored on Nested Row Subsets

Source: R/figure-data-embedding.R
LookupNestedRows.Rd

Per-cell results are often stored only for a subset of a subset of the rows of a sample (for example neighbourhood labels for the defined cells among the counted cells). For records that refer to rows of the full sample table, this returns the stored value, or missing where the row lies outside the subsets.

Usage

LookupNestedRows(
  data,
  sample = "sample",
  row = "row",
  outer,
  inner,
  values = NULL,
  samples,
  outer_name = "counted",
  inner_name = "defined_rows",
  value_name = "cn",
  missing = -1L,
  base = 0L,
  to = "value"
)

Arguments

data

Data frame of records with a sample and a row column.

sample, row

Column names; rows are counted from base.

outer

List (one entry per sample, in the order of samples) of logical vectors over all rows, or lists holding such a vector named outer_name.

inner

List of logical vectors over the outer rows, or lists holding one named inner_name together with the values value_name.

values

Optional list of value vectors over the inner rows (default taken from inner).

samples

Sample names matching the entries of the lists.

outer_name, inner_name, value_name

Element names inside list entries.

missing

Value for rows outside the subsets.

base

Index of the first row (0 for arrays from Python).

to

Name of the new column.

Value

data with the new column.

Examples

d <- data.frame(s = c("a", "a", "b"), r = c(0, 2, 1))
LookupNestedRows(d, "s", "r", outer = list(c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE), c(TRUE, TRUE)),
                 inner = list(c(TRUE, TRUE), c(FALSE, TRUE)),
                 values = list(c(5L, 6L), 7L), samples = c("a", "b"))
#>   s r value
#> 1 a 0     5
#> 2 a 2     6
#> 3 b 1     7
